zh.title: 斯基亞索斯賞機海灘氣流衝擊 兩名遊客受重傷
zh.summary: 兩名遊客於斯基亞索斯海灘遭噴射氣流衝擊受重傷；現場警告標示與圍欄屢遭忽略。
body: 根據 Simple Flying 報導，兩名遊客在斯基亞索斯（Skiathos）著名的賞機海灘遭到離陸噴射客機氣流衝擊，造成兩人身受重傷。事發地點位於斯基亞索斯機場（JSI）周邊，該處為當地知名的航空攝影與賞機景點。
據報導說明，經常有大批人群聚集並沿著斯基亞索斯機場的周界圍欄排隊，目的在於近距離感受離陸噴射客機起飛時所產生的強大噴射氣流。
儘管機場周圍與海灘邊緣均已設置危險警告標示以及防護圍欄，但現場聚集的民眾與觀光客仍屢次忽視這些安全警示標語和阻隔設施，持續於氣流影響範圍內逗留。

en.title: Two Tourists Seriously Injured by Jet Blast at Skiathos Airport (JSI) Beach
en.summary: Two tourists were seriously injured by jet blast at Skiathos while hazard signs were ignored.
body: According to a report published by Simple Flying, two tourists suffered serious injuries after being struck by jet blast at the famous plane-spotting beach situated near Skiathos Airport. The event occurred at the popular viewing area adjacent to the airport boundary.

Crowds of spectators regularly gather and line the perimeter of Skiathos Airport to feel departing jets. Hazard signs and safety barriers have been installed along the perimeter to warn the public of dangers associated with aircraft operations.
However, these hazard signs and protective barriers are repeatedly ignored by individuals lining the airfield boundary to experience the blast from departing jet aircraft.

zh.title: 俄羅斯人工智慧攻擊無人機襲擊烏克蘭紮波羅熱致三人死亡
zh.summary: 一架由人工智慧自主導航的俄軍無人機襲擊烏克蘭紮波羅熱，造成三名平民死亡。
body: 根據《紐約時報》於2026年8月24日發布的調查報導，一架完全由人工智慧導航與選擇目標的俄羅斯「閃電」（Molniya）固定翼攻擊無人機，於2026年7月6日在烏克蘭東南部紮波羅熱（Zaporizhzhia）的一座加油站發動襲擊，造成三名平民死亡。受害者分別為19歲的紮波羅熱國立大學會計系學生特蒂亞娜·布比內茨（Tetiana Bubynets）、41歲的奧列克西·斯維林（Oleksiy Svirin）以及48歲的羅曼·卡爾皮伊（Roman Karpiy）。布比內茨送醫後不治，斯維林與卡爾皮伊隨後亦因傷勢過重身亡。
檢視殘骸的烏克蘭防空指揮官、無人機專家與法醫調查人員表示，該架無人機在飛行過程中完全未依賴無線電控制。該無人機為參與當日襲擊的約六架飛行器之一，整組無人機均未發射可偵測的無線電控制訊號。這種缺乏活性干擾鏈的特徵，大幅降低了旨在切斷飛行員與無人機聯繫的烏軍電子作戰系統效益。
調查人員在回收的機體上並未發現無線電控制天線。對機上未加密的輝達（Nvidia）Jetson Orin微型電腦進行分析後，研究人員發現了存儲的地形影像與目標識別軟體。烏克蘭專家指出，該系統透過比對視覺地標與預設航線進行自主導航，其目標識別軟體則經過訓練，專門用於識別特定類別的物件，當時預定攻擊目標極可能為加油站內存放的丙烷儲氣罐。
該系統超越了過去僅在攻擊最後階段由軟體接管的「最後一哩路」自主技術。在7月6日的襲擊中，該架「閃電」無人機自行導航至目標區域並搜尋符合特徵的物件，無需操作員即時傳送指令或進行最終目標指定。然而，該無人機飛行時未能越過加油站旁的一棟公寓大樓，撞擊牆面後在附近躲避的平民旁爆炸。
輝達公司證實殘骸照片中的硬體為Jetson Orin模組，並說明該產品為針對學生、開發者與新創公司設計的商業級硬體，非軍規設備。回收組件上的標示顯示其產地為中國。專家指出，此起事件可能是首起經證實由機載人工智慧完全自主導航並造成平民死亡的俄羅斯無人機攻擊案例。

en.title: Russian Attack Drone Guided Entirely by AI Kills Three Civilians in Ukraine
en.summary: A Russian AI-guided attack drone struck Zaporizhzhia in Ukraine, killing three civilians sheltering near a gas station.
body: According to an investigation published by The New York Times on August 24, 2026, a Russian Molniya fixed-wing attack drone operating with onboard artificial intelligence killed three civilians in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, on July 6, 2026. The victims of the strike at a gas station were identified as Tetiana Bubynets, a 19-year-old accounting student at Zaporizhzhia National University, Oleksiy Svirin, 41, and Roman Karpiy, 48. Bubynets was pronounced dead at a hospital, while Svirin and Karpiy later succumbed to their injuries.

Ukrainian air-defense commanders, drone specialists, and forensic investigators who examined the wreckage concluded that the aircraft flew without active radio control. The drone was one of approximately six aircraft involved in the attack, and the formation emitted no detectable radio-control signals. This lack of active RF links limited the effectiveness of Ukrainian electronic-warfare systems, which typically disrupt communications between remote pilots and attack drones.

Investigators found no radio-control antenna on the recovered airframe. Further examination of the drone's unencrypted Nvidia Jetson Orin minicomputer provided evidence of autonomous operation. Ukrainian specialists analyzed stored terrain imagery used by the system to navigate by comparing visual landmarks against a preprogrammed flight route. Additionally, the target-recognition software had been specifically trained to recognize categories of objects, likely targeting propane tanks stored at the gas station.

The system represents an advancement beyond "last-mile" autonomy, in which a human operator selects a target before onboard software takes over the final moments of flight. In the July 6 strike, the Molniya drone navigated to the target area and searched for matching visual profiles without real-time human intervention or final human designation. However, the aircraft failed to clear an apartment building adjacent to the gas station, struck a wall, and exploded close to people sheltering nearby.

Nvidia confirmed that photos of the recovered unit showed a Jetson Orin module. The company noted that the component is a commercial product intended for software developers, students, and startups, rather than purpose-built military hardware. Markings on the recovered module indicated that it was manufactured in China. Experts noted that this incident likely represents the first documented case of an AI-guided Russian drone causing civilian deaths.
